module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 43

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/43](https://www.erdosproblems.com/43)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos43

/--
Let $f(N)$ be the maximum possible size of a Sidon set in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$.
-/
noncomputable abbrev f (N : ℕ) : ℕ := Finset.maxSidonSubsetCard (Finset.Icc 1 N)

/--
If $A$ and $B$ are Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, is it true that
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}\leq\binom{f(N)}{2}+O(1)?$$

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page notes that this follows from the solution to
Erdős Problem 42.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_43.parts.i : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ C : ℝ, ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
      IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) →
      (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} →
      ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤ ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ) + C := by
  sorry

/--
If $A$ and $B$ are equal-sized Sidon sets in $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with
$(A-A)\cap(B-B)=\{0\}$, can the bound be improved to
$$\binom{\lvert A\rvert}{2}+\binom{\lvert B\rvert}{2}
    \leq (1-c+o(1))\binom{f(N)}{2}$$
for some constant $c>0$?

The answer is no; the Erdős Problems page records a negative answer due to Barreto.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5 11]
theorem erdos_43.parts.ii : answer(False) ↔
    ∃ᵉ (c > 0), ∃ o : ℕ → ℝ, o =o[Filter.atTop] (1 : ℕ → ℝ) ∧
    ∀ᶠ N in Filter.atTop, ∀ (A B : Finset ℕ),
      A ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      B ⊆ Finset.Icc 1 N →
      IsSidon (A : Set ℕ) →
      IsSidon (B : Set ℕ) →
      A.card = B.card →
      (A - A) ∩ (B - B) = {0} →
      ((A.card.choose 2 + B.card.choose 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) ≤
        (1 - c + o N) * ((f N).choose 2 : ℝ) := by
  sorry

end Erdos43

reformulations.difference: The difference sets use truncated subtraction on ℕ, whereas the source uses ordinary signed integer differences.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: This does not change the condition that the intersection equals {0}. For nonempty sets, natural self-differences consist of zero and the positive integer self-differences. Integer self-difference sets are symmetric under negation, so a shared negative difference exists exactly when a shared positive difference exists. If either set is empty, both versions fail the equality. The exact iff after embedding the finsets into ℤ was proved in /workspace/review/natdiff.lean, together with preservation of the Sidon property and cardinality.

reformulations.difference: As in part i, the disjoint-difference hypothesis is expressed using natural-number subtraction rather than signed integer subtraction.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The natural and integer intersection-equals-{0} conditions are equivalent for all finite A and B, including empty sets, by the proved lemma Review43.nat_int_difference_condition. Embedding into ℤ also preserves the Sidon property and cardinalities, hence the equal-size hypothesis and both sides of the bound are unchanged.

sources_consulted: Mathlib/Analysis/Asymptotics/Defs.lean and Lemmas.lean — IsLittleO and isLittleO_one_iff
review.notes: Checked all three declarations. A sorry-free Lean proof confirms that f is the attained maximum Sidon-subset cardinality. Boundary checks include f(0)=0, f(1)=1, empty sets, and satisfiability of both theorems' hypotheses for every N≥1; exhaustive finite tests covered N≤10. The constants and error function have the required uniform scope, and the little-o condition is equivalent to convergence to zero. Both research-solved tags and answer(False) values agree with the source: part i follows from Problem 42, and part ii is disproved by Barreto's asymptotic construction.
